title: Starter kit: code path-to-prod + pricing & microcopy experiments
content:
Goal:
Deliver a compact "starter kit" messaging bundle that ties a minute-to-demo technical path (repo -> run locally -> deploy sandbox) to clear pricing language and microcopy hooks that maximise developer activation and reduce surprise billing.

Audience:
- Individual engineers evaluating APIs for prototype/POC work
- Small product teams who need to ship a feature in 1–2 sprints
- Platform/infra leads who evaluate vendor economics for pilot workloads

Topline one-liners to A/B:
- "Ship an LLM feature from local repo to production sandbox in under 45 minutes — predictable cost, no surprise token bills."
- "Start free, scale with committed bursts — pay for the compute you use, not the mystery."
- "Developer-first inference: predictable latency, transparent unit pricing, deploy anywhere."

Value prop pillars (developer-focused framing):
1) Quick-to-build: code-first quickstart with a single repo (starter-kit.zip) and CLI script that wires up the first call. Keep copy: "Clone, npm install, run demo."
2) Predictable economics: show an explicit worked example (50k tokens/day -> $X/mo at recommended settings). Use plain phrases: "tokens are billed per 1k generated tokens; request overhead capped and shown in the console."
3) Safe experimentation: sandbox mode with a low-cost, capped quota and automatic escalation rules. Microcopy: "Start sandbox — no live keys, safe-by-default."
4) Performance clarity: surface median p50/p95 latency for the developer's region and model combo in the console. Copy: "Expected latency: ~120ms (p50) — real measured from your account."

Quickstart angle (‘Code path to prod’) — steps to surface in UI + docs:
- Step 0: Starter kit zip (starter-kit.zip) on landing page: files: README, quickstart.js, docker-compose.dev, infra/ (sample minimal deploy to sandbox).
- Step 1: Clone + run locally ("npm run demo") -> displays sample chat + cost preview overlay.
- Step 2: Click "Create sandbox" from the demo overlay -> auto-provisioned key with 10k free tokens and safe limits.
- Step 3: One-click deploy to sandbox (Terraform snippet populated) -> show estimated monthly cost card before confirm.
- Step 4: Promote sandbox to a staging key (commit + policy) -> shows commit diff and projected cost at scale.

Pricing-language drafts (plain, developer-friendly):
- Headline: "Metered per-inference compute — predictable, transparent."
- Small explainer: "You pay for generated tokens and for optional dedicated compute. Hosted API default: per-1k generated tokens + fixed request overhead. Dedicated pools: flat hourly capacity + per-token usage at a discounted rate."
- Sandbox offering: "Every account gets a sandbox credit pool (10k tokens) — safe by default. Sandbox keys are rate-limited and will not be charged to your billing account until you upgrade."
- Burst semantics: "Burst credits let you exceed reserved capacity for short periods. Unused burst credits expire monthly."
- Example micro-pricing snippet (for illustration in docs, not final): "Estimate: small chat bot (50k tokens/day) ≈ $120/month (hosted API, opt-in caching)."

Microcopy and CTA experiments (UI + emails):
- Button: "Run demo (10k free tokens)" vs "Try in Sandbox (no card)"
- Banner: "Starter kit: clone + run in 2 commands — see pricing before you deploy"
- Welcome email subject lines to boost activation:
  - "Your Redwood starter kit — run the demo with 10k tokens"
  - "See how much your first 1M tokens will cost — quick calculator inside"
- Onboarding tooltip text: "Toggle caching to reduce token spend — try before you commit."

Competitive notes (quick read for GTM):
- Competitor A (general cloud AI): emphasises model catalog + enterprise contracts; weakness: opaque request overheads and billing units. Opportunity: call out our explicit per-request overhead and cost preview in the console.
- Competitor B (API-first model vendor): very simple free tier but limited throughput and no sandbox to simulate scale. Opportunity: we offer sandbox + burst credits + a code path that includes infra snippets.
- Competitor C (self-host runtimes): strong on control but high ops cost. Positioning: "Get self-host economics without hiring a serving team — predictable per-token pricing, optional dedicated pools."

Sample quick copy differentiators to use in pitch decks and emails:
- "Predictable, developer-friendly pricing — see the cost before you deploy."
- "Sandbox that mirrors production performance and billing — test safely."
- "From repo to sandbox to staging in one developer flow."

Measurement plan (what to track for experiments):
- Activation funnel metrics: repo-clone -> run demo -> create sandbox (goal: conversion rate from clone to sandbox >= 20%)
- Time-to-first-successful-request (target < 45 minutes)
- First-week usage: tokens consumed, feature flags toggled (caching on/off)
- Customer support triggers: number of billing-related tickets opened in first 14 days (lower is better)
- Average invoice surprise score (qualitative tag on tickets)

Experiment matrix (initial A/B candidates):
- A: CTA copy "Run demo (10k free tokens)" vs B: "Try in Sandbox (no card)" -> track sandbox creation rate and time-to-first-request.
- A: Pricing line itemized (tokens + overhead) vs B: blended per-1k price -> track questions to support and conversion to paid.
- A: Show estimated cost card pre-deploy vs B: show only post-deploy -> track drop-offs at confirm step.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Finalize token-per-unit math for each curated model — need input from applied-ml on typical generation ratios for chat vs completion. (Action: @Diego to pull sample traces)
- Sandbox scaling: should sandbox simulate p95 latency at 50% of production? Ops input required. (Action: SRE sync)
- Exact free sandbox token amount — proposed: 10k; discuss tradeoffs.
- Legal: do we need to mark sandbox usage in TOS differently? (Legal review requested)

Copy samples for docs section (intended to be drop-in):
- Quickstart header: "Starter kit: your first inference in 2 minutes — demo, sandbox, and cost preview."
- Pricing blurb: "Transparent billing: you’re charged for generated tokens and an optional compute layer. Use sandbox credits to experiment without a card."

Appendix: small worked example to show in UI (for engineers):
- Scenario: simple summarization endpoint, average 120 tokens generated per request, 1k requests/day -> 120k tokens/day -> 3.6M tokens/month. With caching and batch settings suggested in Optimize, expected bill = $Y (show calculator).

Notes to self: keep language concrete, avoid abstract "efficiency" claims without numbers, and prioritise tooling that shows cost before you sign up for a key.

References / links: see linked artifacts for starter repo + Confluence on onboarding experiments.
